user.title: Connect to Tuxedo Touch
user.description: Enter the panel's web login credentials (not your 4-digit keypad user code, unless your installer set them to match).

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Tuxedo Touch unit on your LAN. When Home Assistant is on the same network segment, the panel is identified by its MAC address and a changed address is a reconfigure; otherwise it is identified by this address, so give it a static IP or DHCP reservation.
data_description.use_https: Required if 'Secured Web Server Access' is enabled on the unit (the common/default state).
data_description.username: The unit's web login username (touchscreen: Settings -> Login settings), not the keypad code.
data_description.code: Optional. Used as the default arm/disarm code so automations can arm without prompting.
data_description.partition: The panel partition this entry controls.
data_description.port: The web server port on the unit. 443 with HTTPS enabled (the default state), 80 without.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate Tuxedo Touch
reauth_confirm.description: The panel at {host} rejected the stored web login credentials. Enter the current ones.

data_description.username: The web login username from the touchscreen's Login settings.
data_description.password: The web login password for that account.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Tuxedo Touch
reconfigure.description: Change the panel's address, port, credentials, keypad code or partition. Leave the password and keypad code blank to keep the stored ones.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Tuxedo Touch unit on your LAN. When Home Assistant is on the same network segment, the panel is identified by its MAC address and a changed address is a reconfigure; otherwise it is identified by this address, so give it a static IP or DHCP reservation.
data_description.use_https: Required if 'Secured Web Server Access' is enabled on the unit (the common/default state).
data_description.username: The unit's web login username (touchscreen: Settings -> Login settings), not the keypad code.
data_description.password: The unit's web login password. Blank keeps the stored password.
data_description.code: Optional. Used as the default arm/disarm code so automations can arm without prompting. Blank keeps the stored code.
data_description.partition: The panel partition this entry controls.
data_description.port: The web server port on the unit. 443 with HTTPS enabled (the default state), 80 without.

error.invalid_auth: Invalid username or password. If the panel was recently reset, web access may have been disabled for this user - re-enable it on the touchscreen under Setup -> Account.
error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect - check the IP/port and that the unit is reachable. The panel serves only ONE connection at a time, so close any browser tab open to it and retry.
error.panel_error: The panel answered but the response could not be used. See the Home Assistant log for the specific reason.
error.unknown: Unexpected error - see the Home Assistant log for the traceback

abort.another_panel: That address answers as a different panel than this entry was set up for.
abort.unknown_panel: That DHCP lease is for a MAC address no Tuxedo Touch entry was set up with.

no_code.message: No alarm code provided and none configured for this panel.

auth_failed.message: The panel rejected the stored web login credentials: {error}

update_failed.message: Could not read the panel's status: {error}

https_required.message: The panel redirected the API call to HTTPS. Turn on 'Use HTTPS' for this entry; the repair notification does it for you.

confirm.title: Switch {title} to HTTPS
confirm.description: 'Secured Web Server Access' is enabled on the panel, so it redirects every plain-HTTP API call to HTTPS and arming, disarming and status all fail. Submitting this turns on 'Use HTTPS' for this entry, moves port 80 to 443 (port {port} stays as it is if it is anything else) and reloads the integration.

abort.entry_gone: That Tuxedo Touch entry no longer exists, so there is nothing left to switch.

duplicate_entry.title: Two Tuxedo Touch entries reach one panel
duplicate_entry.description: '{title}' and '{other}' both reach the same panel and partition by different addresses, so only one of them can hold the panel's identity. Remove whichever entry you do not want under Settings > Devices & services; the other adopts the panel's MAC address on its next start.
